clue.text: Reported European drug smuggling in Charlie, for instance?

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the word for a European is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a Czech is a European, and the word sounds like check

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside, so one piece is concealed within another

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, a drug

explanation.surface: A news report about a European caught bringing narcotics into a city, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Checkpoint Charlie was the Berlin Wall crossing; the question mark flags Charlie as just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkpoint Charlie was the famous Berlin Wall crossing between East and West, so it is one example of the kind.

clue.text: Nail in strips put up in English city

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the letters are raised, reading from bottom to top
in places the catching word inside the word for strips

parts.note: slats are thin strips of wood
to nail someone is to catch them, to nab

explanation.surface: A carpenter fixing a nail into slats of wood somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nail' is a verb, catch, not hardware; 'put up' reads the whole assembly from the bottom of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hertfordshire cathedral city named after Britain's first Christian martyr, Alban.

clue.text: Try to look, as a searcher

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to ogle is to look, especially lustfully

explanation.surface: An instruction to someone hunting for something to have a look around.
explanation.definitionFit: The web search engine is a familiar tool people use when searching online.

clue.text: See 8
Business partners, a hundred strip off for the recruits

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
N and S, north and south, are partners at the bridge table
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or spoiled, so the letters of strip are rearranged

explanation.surface: Office colleagues and a hundred others strip off in front of new army intake.
explanation.walkthrough: At the bridge table North and South play as partners, a convention setters use often.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts are people compulsorily enlisted, so they are military recruits.

clue.text: Bird sees sign beginning to wobble in terrible gale

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters are thrown into disorder, mixed up together

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bird watcher sees a signpost start to shake in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' and 'in' are linking words; LEO plus W go in with GALE and 'terrible' mixes all eight letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle owl is a very large owl of Europe and Asia, a species of bird.

clue.text: Connection in which hands held?

definitions.meaning: a structure linking two places is a link or connection
the card game in which players hold hands of thirteen cards

explanation.surface: A link where people hold hands, like a lovers' walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The hands are hands of cards, not people's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A span over a river connects its banks; the card game is played with dealt hands.

clue.text: White to satisfy clothes for Covent Garden favourite

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, meaning one word wraps around another

parts.note: to slake is to satisfy, as with thirst
wan means pale or white-faced

explanation.surface: Pale garments bought to please a fashion-conscious shopper in Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb. Covent Garden is home to London's Royal Opera House, where the Royal Ballet performs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet is a perennial favourite of the Royal Ballet's repertoire at Covent Garden.

clue.text: Contentious issue with which to juggle?

definitions.meaning: a controversial matter nobody wants to handle
something too scalding to hold, tossed from hand to hand

explanation.surface: A tricky debate that politicians juggle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a controversial subject; literally a scalding tuber you would pass quickly between your hands.

clue.text: Director has dismissed head of school

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for school is sacked, removed from the front

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A film director has sacked a headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director' is not a film-maker but something that points the way. Harrow is a famous English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign shaped like a pointer directs people which way to go.

clue.text: Good to join the dots, then picture finally showing European city

indicators.note: to join means a letter enters among the dots, sitting inside them

parts.note: a colon is the punctuation mark made of two dots

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of picture

explanation.surface: A dot-to-dot puzzle completed to reveal a picture of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes into COLON, the two-dot punctuation mark, then the last letter of 'picture'.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city on the Rhine, Köln, is known in English by this name.

clue.text: Old sultan unfortunately recalled racket

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for unfortunately runs backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
a din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: A historical sultan regretfully remembered for a noisy disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns ALAS into SALA.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth-century Muslim ruler of Egypt and Syria who fought the Crusaders was a sultan.

clue.text: Why might the earth have moved, when soft testicle on cat stimulated?

definitions.text: Why might the earth have moved

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: stimulated means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saucy question about the earth moving during an indelicate scene involving a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The earth moved' is a jokey phrase for sexual ecstasy, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological theory of shifting crustal slabs explains earthquakes and continental drift.

clue.text: Pink boxes opening, showing material

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: Pink packaging opened to reveal fabric inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' is the adjective sense, physical, not cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily or physical, as material things are, rather than spiritual.

clue.text: Queen wearing bra, I suspect, among endless goods one's handled in a shop

indicators.note: among puts one assembled piece between the letters of the trimmed goods word
endless means the final letter is cut off the word for goods

parts.note: cargo is goods carried by ship or plane

indicators.note: wearing means the royal letters are clothed by the rearranged bra and I
suspect suggests the letters are not to be trusted as they stand and must be rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen in a bra, seen among items handled in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' makes RIBA; with the royal letters inside it becomes RIERBA, set within the cut-down goods word, CARG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag with handles given to shoppers to carry purchases.

clue.text: Hedonist, after crossing river, gathering thoughts, initially

indicators.note: crossing means the word for after lies across, around, the river piece

parts.note: later means after

indicators.note: gathering means the river collects a letter within it

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of thoughts

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker crosses a river while collecting his thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in northern England. 'initially' applies only to 'thoughts'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey, lotus-fruit consumers lived in dreamy indulgence, so the term means a pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: Pet silencer working fast — that should keep the little pests away

definitions.text: that should keep the little pests away

indicators.note: working means in operation, so these letters are put into a new working order

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A device to quieten a noisy pet, working quickly to keep pests at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges PET SILENCER into INSECTREPEL; 'fast' is a noun, Lent, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray or cream that deters mosquitoes and other bugs, the little pests.

clue.text: Someone in the casino, one upset about nothing, winning

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a crier is one who weeps, someone upset
O is zero, nothing
up means ahead, winning

explanation.surface: A gambler who loses everything sits upset beside a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is not a reversal signal here: 'one upset' is a person who weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: The croupier runs a gaming table, dealing cards or spinning the roulette wheel.

clue.text: A criminal charged? That's shocking!

parts.note: a ... is a receiver of stolen goods, so a charged criminal is a ... with current running through it, which gives a shock

explanation.surface: Outrage at a lawbreaker being prosecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' means electrically live, not accused, and 'criminal' is a fence, a handler of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier carrying current that shocks livestock or intruders who touch it.

clue.text: See 13
Customer from the East invested in the same on wood?

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the compass letter is put within the name

parts.note: the same refers back to East, so East plus wood gives Eastwood; the actor Clint Eastwood supplies his first name

explanation.surface: A customer from the Orient puts money into the same timber business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' repeats East: East on wood is Eastwood, so the first name wanted is the actor's, CLINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a person buying services, a customer.

clue.text: Military vehicles go fast, stopping abruptly reversing past bird, say?

indicators.note: past means coming after, so the reversed piece follows the bird's letter
say signals that the bird's name is heard as a letter

parts.note: a jay is a bird whose name sounds like the letter J

indicators.note: reversing means the trimmed word runs backwards
stopping abruptly cuts off the last letter, an abrupt end

parts.note: to speed is to go fast

explanation.surface: Army trucks speeding, braking hard and reversing past a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping abruptly' leaves SPEE, and 'reversing' turns that to EEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugged four-wheel-drive vehicle was developed for the US army in WWII.

clue.text: The capital of a US state? Have you any idea, roughly speaking?

definitions.text: The capital of a US state?

indicators.note: roughly speaking signals a loose sound-alike, said aloud

parts.note: have you any idea is colloquially d'you know

explanation.surface: A quiz question met with a baffled 'have you any idea?'
explanation.walkthrough: D'you know, said casually, sounds like the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the state capital of Alaska.

clue.text: Cheerful as a golfer?

definitions.meaning: a golfer who plays a short lofted chip shot

explanation.surface: A happy golfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper means bright and cheerful; a golfer who chips onto the green is one who chips.

clue.text: Strike off this, it's unplanned

definitions.meaning: to hit with the open hand, a slap
the idiom off the ... means improvised or unplanned, so this is the shirt part

explanation.surface: Something struck off as unplanned.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a light blow is to strike; the sleeve end appears in the idiom for improvised speech.

clue.text: Wrong skill shown by a backing singer

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so skill and a read in reverse

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A backing singer showing poor technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing singer' splits: 'backing' turns ART A into ATRA, and 'singer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, the American crooner, was a famous singer.

clue.text: Written in visa, temporary stuff

indicators.note: written in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A temporary visa with stuff written in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is a verb: to fill up.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to fill to capacity, as when stuffing oneself with food.

clue.text: See 18
Bring about fifty in to Asia, cute bats

indicators.note: in places the Roman fifty inside the jumbled letters
bats means crazy, so the letters of Asia and cute go haywire

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty cute bats being brought to Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' is the adjective crazy, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To actualise something is to make it real, to bring it into being.
